mcqs.title: Preserving an axis
mcqs.stem: An array `units` has shape (3, 4), with stores in rows and products in columns. What are the shapes of `units[:, 1]` and `units[:, 1:2]`, respectively?
mcqs.rationale: An integer column index removes that axis. A one-column slice preserves its length-one axis; both retain all three stores.

mcqs.title: One multiplier per store
mcqs.stem: A revenue array has shape (3, 4). A vector `factors` has shape (3,), containing one multiplier for each store (row). Which expression applies the correct factor to every product in each store?
mcqs.rationale: A (3, 1) factor array matches the three store rows and broadcasts along the four product columns. The other expressions have incompatible trailing sizes 4 and 3.

mcqs.title: Interpreting totals
mcqs.stem: A revenue array has shape (3, 4), with stores in rows and products in columns. What does `revenue.sum(axis=1)` return?

options.text: A (3,) vector with one total per store.
A (4,) vector with one total per product.
One scalar total across every entry.

mcqs.rationale: Summing along axis 1 removes the product axis and retains one total for each of the three stores.

mcqs.title: Values, positions, and ties
mcqs.stem: For `revenue = np.array([[60., 40.], [60., 30.]])`, what do `revenue.max()` and `np.argmax(revenue)` return, and how is the tie handled?

options.text: Both return 60; neither can identify a position.
The maximum is 60 and argmax is 2, because the last tied occurrence wins.
The maximum is 60 and argmax returns both coordinates (0, 0) and (1, 0).
The maximum is 60 and argmax is 0, the first position in row-major flattened order.

mcqs.rationale: max returns the value. With no axis, argmax returns the first flattened position at the maximum. argwhere(revenue == revenue.max()) can identify all tied coordinates.

rubric.evidence: 1 point: attributes and axis meanings; 1: predictions and results for integer versus sliced column selection; 1: first-two-store/last-two-product slice, shape, and explanation.

1 point: units times prices with operand/result shapes; 1: dollar-unit and per-product explanation; 1: explains why (3, 4) times (3,) fails; 1: correct column-shaped factors, adjusted revenue, and per-store interpretation.

1 point: unadjusted totals by store and product with names, shapes, and units; 1: minimum/maximum store positions, names, and totals; 1: maximum cell value and first coordinate using argmax/unravel_index; 1: all tied coordinates/names and value-versus-position/tie explanation.

1 point: correctly creates view and independent copy before edits and records predictions; 1: displays resulting arrays and explains source sharing versus original preservation; 1: correct row-shaped new-store concatenation from original units; 1: new shape/last row and explanations of matching dimensions and product order.
0.5 point: name and readable code, results, and explanations; 0.5: completion note describing restart/run/save and HTML inspection. The report itself does not prove execution history.
